Unit 3 · AI Lab Sprint · 20 points

Shelf Check

Your first run in Amazon Rekognition, with your team, before you do it alone for your project. Rekognition is a cloud AI service from Amazon Web Services (AWS) that finds and reads text in images.

The situation

Midtown Hardware is a small hardware store. Once a month, staff walk the aisles and type every item number and price into a spreadsheet by hand. It takes two days.

The store manager has asked: could staff take a phone photo of each shelf tag, and let Amazon Rekognition read the numbers instead? The manager is the decision-maker.

Your team tests Rekognition on 15 images from the store and reports what you found. Tonight you use the same method you will use in your Unit 3 project.

Words you need tonight

Key text: the exact text the decision-maker needs from an image, such as 22-9105 $4.99.

SKU (stock keeping unit): the store's item number for a product. QTY on a label means quantity.

Answer key: your list of the correct key text for every image, written before you test.

Confidence score: a number from 0 to 100 that Rekognition reports about its own answer. It is not a promise that the answer is right.

Hit rate: how many images Rekognition read correctly, out of the total.

Hard image: one a careful person can still read, but an AI might not.

These 15 images were made for this sprint. They are drawings made to look like photos. That is fine for practice. For your Unit 3 project, every photo must be one you take yourself.
Step 1

Your team

Your instructor puts you in a team of 3. The 15 images are split into three sets of 5. Each person tests one set on their own laptop, so everyone gets into AWS tonight. Then the team puts all 15 results together.

Team of 2? Each of you takes one set, and you split Set C between you. Team of 4? Two of you share one set: one person types, the other uploads.

Step 2

Start the lab now

The lab takes several minutes to start. Start it first, then write your answer key while you wait.

  1. In LEO, select Content and open the AWS Academy Learner Lab module. Select AWS Virtual Environment, then select the blue AWS Virtual Environment link. The lab opens in a new browser tab. The first time only, scroll to the bottom and accept the Terms and Conditions.
  2. Select Start Lab. The dot next to AWS turns yellow, then green.
  3. Don't wait for the green dot. Go to Step 3 now.
Never select Reset. Use Chrome or Firefox on a laptop, not a phone.
Step 3

Write your answer key before you test

This is the step that keeps a test honest. If you decide what "correct" means after you see what Rekognition read, you will grade it too generously.

What you do: For each image in your set, type the key text exactly as it appears, character for character. Select an image to see it full size. Then mark whether the image is hard, and why. When all 5 are done, select Lock my answer key. Locking records the time. You cannot type test results until your key is locked.
Pick your set in Step 1 first.

All 15 images

Download the 5 images in your set to your laptop. You upload them to Rekognition in Step 4. Your set has an orange border.

Step 4

Test your 5 images in Rekognition

  1. When the dot next to AWS is green, select the word AWS. AWS opens in another tab.
  2. Check that the top right says N. Virginia. If it doesn't, select it and choose US East (N. Virginia).
  3. Type Rekognition in the search bar at the top, press Enter, and select Amazon Rekognition.
  4. In the left menu, under Demos, select Text in image. No menu? Select the three-line icon (☰) at the top left.
  5. Under Use your own image, select Upload or drag and drop and choose one image. The text Rekognition found appears under Results.
  6. For the confidence score, select Response, below Results. Find the entry for your key text that says "Type": "LINE", not WORD. It looks like this:
"DetectedText": "SKU 22-9105",
"Type": "LINE",
"Confidence": 99.31
What you do: For each image, type what Rekognition read for your key text, in the same order as your key, and its confidence score. Leave out words that are not part of your key text, such as SKU or BIN. If your key text is on two lines, type both reads together and use the lower confidence score. If Rekognition found nothing, tick No text found. Record each result before you upload the next image. The new result replaces the old one on the screen.
Screenshot for your turn-in: on one of your images, open Response so the confidence score shows, and take a screenshot of the whole AWS screen. On Windows, press Windows + Shift + S. On a Mac, press Command + Shift + 4.
Lock your answer key in Step 3 first.
Step 5

Put your team's 15 results together

Every team member needs all 15 rows on their own sheet. Share your 5 rows, and add your teammates' rows.

Share my rows

Select Copy my rows, then send the code to your teammates in a chat or email.

Add a teammate's rows

Paste a teammate's code and select Add rows. Or type their rows into the table below as they read them to you.

Your own rows are shaded. To change your own rows, go back to Steps 3 and 4.

Step 6

Your team's results

This part fills in by itself from the table in Step 5.

Team questions

Talk as a team, then each person types the team's answers on their own sheet. Short answers are fine.

Be ready to tell the other site your confident mistake: the image, what Rekognition read, and the confidence score.
Step 7

End the lab and turn in

  1. Go back to the Learner Lab tab and select End Lab.
  2. Select Print at the top of this page. In the print window, choose Save as PDF (Portable Document Format) and save it. The PDF has your answer key, your team's table, the results, and your answers.
  3. Upload three files to the Unit 3 AI Lab Sprint dropbox in LEO:
    • The PDF of this page
    • Your screenshot of the Rekognition Response panel
    • Your AI Use Disclosure Form
Every team member uploads. Each person turns in their own PDF and their own screenshot. Your answers save on this laptop, so you can come back and print later.
